headline: 17M AT 1.32% Li2O: Li-FT POWER EXPANDS NORTH AMERICA'S LARGEST SPODUMENE DEPOSIT IN NWT (TSXV:LIFT)
snippet: Li-FT Power Ltd. (TSXV:LIFT / ASX:LFT / OTCQX:LIFFF) released drill results on June 30, 2026 from 20 holes totalling 5,324 metres across the 2026 winter and 2025 summer programs at the Yellowknife Lithium Project in the Northwest Territories. Best results include YLP-0320: 17 metres at 1.32% Li2O and YLP-0304: 21 metres at 1.09% Li2O including 13 metres at 1.38% Li2O, adding to a consolidated inferred Mineral Resource of 50.4 million tonnes at 1.00% Li2O (506,000 tonnes Li2O / 1.25 million tonnes LCE) — the largest spodumene pegmatite project in North America. The 2026 summer drill program is currently underway with further assays pending.

headline: MIDNIGHT SUN CONFIRMS 6.7KM OF CONTINUOUS COPPER AT DUMBWA — 260+ HOLES, 56,855M DRILLED IN ZAMBIA COPPERBELT (TSXV:MMA)
snippet: Midnight Sun Mining Corp. (TSXV:MMA / OTCQB:MDNGF) announced June 29, 2026 that 77 additional holes at the wholly owned Dumbwa copper deposit in Solwezi, Zambia confirm continuous near-surface sulphide copper mineralization across 6.7 kilometres of strike at widths of 600 to 1,000 metres — now totalling 260-plus holes and 56,855 metres drilled. Five rigs continue northward along the trend with approximately 12,500 metres remaining in Phase One, targeting the full planned 11.5-kilometre strike extent with completion expected in Q3 2026. A technical webinar with COO Dr. Kevin Bonel was held June 30 to discuss results and exploration scale.

headline: SILVER POSTS 6TH STRAIGHT ANNUAL DEFICIT AT 46.3M OZ — PRICE DOWN 39% FROM $123 JANUARY PEAK AS FED HAWKISHNESS WINS
snippet: Silver's structural supply deficit widened for the sixth consecutive year in 2026, reaching 46.3 million ounces according to the Silver Institute's World Silver Survey — up from 40.3 million ounces in 2025 and representing a cumulative 762 million ounces drained from above-ground inventories since 2021. Despite this persistent tightness, silver is trading near US$58-60 per ounce as of June 30 — down approximately 39% from January 2026's all-time high near US$123 — as Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish policy stance and a stronger U.S. dollar overwhelm the physical supply signal. Silver has now posted seven consecutive weekly losses, a sentiment extreme that has historically marked major accumulation opportunities in the metal's structural bull markets.

headline: VIRGINIA SAVES BULLION TAX EXEMPTION AT MIDNIGHT — GOV. SPANBERGER SIGNS EXTENSION TO 2028 HOURS BEFORE SUNSET DEADLINE
snippet: Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger signed the state's biennium budget bill (HB30) on June 30, 2026 — hours before a midnight deadline — extending the sales tax exemption on gold, silver, and platinum bullion and legal tender coins through 2028 and preventing a July 1 re-imposition of the tax. The Sound Money Defense League and Money Metals Exchange coordinated a grassroots campaign that persuaded legislators to embed the extension in the budget bill; without passage, Virginia would have become one of the few U.S. states actively taxing precious metals purchases while simultaneously triggering a state government shutdown. The result is a direct policy win for retail bullion investors in one of the eastern seaboard's largest markets.

headline: TERBIUM +22.8% IN JUNE TO $969/KG, GERMANIUM HITS 2026 RECORD AT $2,674/KG — CHINA EXPORT CONTROLS SQUEEZE HEAVY RARE EARTHS
snippet: The rare earth market delivered a split verdict in June 2026: heavy rare earths led by terbium surged 22.8% to $969.69 per kilogram while germanium extended its 2026 run to a new record of $2,673.66/kg domestic China — approximately 30% above April's $2,049/kg — with Western in-warehouse germanium now at $6,150/kg. China controls an estimated 98-99% of refined heavy rare earth supply including terbium and dysprosium, and the pace of Chinese export licence approvals has been running well below western demand since restrictions were tightened in 2025. Light rare earths staged a meaningful recovery from April's steep pullback, while the structural supply deficit underpinning the multi-year price move remains intact on sustained EV motor, defence, and wind turbine demand.

headline: KORYX DRILLS 714M AT 0.31% CuEq AT HAIB — 14 RIGS ADVANCE 744MT NAMIBIA PORPHYRY TOWARD LATE-2026 PFS (TSXV:KRY)
snippet: Koryx Copper Inc. (TSXV:KRY) released further infill assays from 15 holes (5,351 metres) at the wholly owned Haib Copper Project in southern Namibia on June 29, 2026, confirming wide, grade-consistent copper-molybdenum-gold mineralisation — highlighted by hole HM153 returning 714 metres at 0.31% CuEq from surface (101 ppm Mo, 0.018 g/t Au), at or above the March 2026 Mineral Resource average of 744 million measured and indicated tonnes at 0.28% copper. With 14 drill rigs now turning simultaneously on-site to upgrade inferred resources to indicated confidence, Koryx is targeting a prefeasibility study in late 2026 for a 92,000 tpa copper concentrate operation over a planned 24-year open-pit mine life — one of the largest undeveloped porphyry copper projects outside of North and South America.

headline: DOUBLEVIEW HAT MINERALIZATION EXTENDS 150M EAST — BC Cu-Co-Sc-Au-Ag PROJECT ADVANCES TOWARD 2027 MRE AND PFS (TSXV:DBG)
snippet: Doubleview Gold Corp. (TSXV:DBG / OTCQB:DBLVF) announced June 29, 2026 that recent drilling at the Hat Project in northwestern British Columbia has extended mineralisation approximately 150 metres east beyond the current resource envelope — confirmed by June 9 assays from holes H102 through H108 — and that ongoing drilling continues to de-risk the deposit in support of an updated Mineral Resource Estimate targeted for early 2027 and advancing Pre-Feasibility Study planning. Hat is distinguished by a five-metal production profile (copper, cobalt, scandium, gold, silver) with a projected first-decade average of 74,000 tonnes Cu, 254,000 oz Au, 376,000 oz Ag, and 2,700 tonnes Co annually — combining energy-transition exposure with defence-critical mineral leverage independent of copper price alone.

headline: URANIUM LONG-TERM CONTRACTS BREACH $94/LB FOR FIRST TIME SINCE 2008 — WIDENING SPREAD OVER $84-87 SPOT SIGNALS UTILITY BUYING
snippet: Uranium long-term contract prices have breached US$94 per pound for the first time since 2008 — well above the US$84-87/lb spot range that prevailed throughout Q2 2026 — creating a widening spread that historically signals utilities locking in supply ahead of anticipated tightening. Q2 spot entered at US$84.19 and consolidated in a narrow range after January's US$101 high. Sprott Asset Management CEO John Ciampaglia projects supply pressures will intensify significantly into the early 2030s as the global reactor fleet expands and uranium mine development timelines lengthen; physical uranium funds have continued to absorb available spot supply throughout the quarter, supporting the floor. The term-market breakout mirrors the configuration seen in 2006-2007 that preceded the sector's most dramatic price surge.

headline: WHEN WILL THE BLEEDING STOP? SILVER POSTS 7TH STRAIGHT WEEKLY LOSS AS GOLD TESTS $4,000 — MONEY METALS EXAMINES THE SETUP
snippet: Money Metals Exchange's June 29, 2026 market commentary examines when the relentless precious metals correction may exhaust itself — with gold losing more than 2% and silver falling more than 8% in the prior week alone, and silver now posting its seventh consecutive weekly decline from January's all-time high. The analysis argues that Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish pivot, the June 15 U.S.-Iran ceasefire eliminating the geopolitical premium, and sustained dollar strength have combined to create a sentiment extreme that has historically preceded sharp reversals in the metals complex, and that investors accumulating physical silver at current prices near US$58 are buying into a structural six-year supply deficit at the lowest prices since late 2025.

headline: GOLDSEEK: MINING STOCKS NOW BETTER THAN BUYING GOLD — DIVERGENCE FROM METALS MIRRORS EVERY MAJOR ENTRY IN THIS BULL CYCLE
snippet: A GoldSeek technical analysis published in late June 2026 argues that quality mining equities are presenting a materially better risk-reward entry than buying physical gold or silver directly, with several producers and developers holding above June 17 support levels while silver has corrected approximately 50% from January's US$123 all-time high — a divergence that has historically signalled the best accumulation windows in this cycle. The author identifies a potential major low forming in the near term, with a subsequent rally projected to produce larger percentage gains in mining stocks than in the underlying metals — noting that the current setup of extreme speculator shorts, compressed valuations, and over-extended sentiment precisely mirrors previous major low setups at October 2022 and the Q1 2024 base.
